children.name: This project was a travel-style promotional poster designed for the Mercedes-Benz Classic Center to celebrate their move to Long Beach, CA and spotlight one of their restored vehicles, the G55 Cabrio. The goal was to create a printed 12 x 18 inch poster in CMYK that blended brand heritage with a sense of adventure, using a U.S. travel destination to frame the story visually. Hawaii’s volcanic landscape became the setting, pairing naturally with the rugged character of the G-Class. The poster needed to both inform viewers of the center’s new location and capture attention with a bold, aspirational image rooted in Mercedes-Benz’s identity.

I explored the Classic Center’s audience, Mercedes-Benz heritage, state-specific visuals, Art Deco references, vintage automotive posters, and the engineering history of the G55 Cabrio. children.name: Spierer University is a fictional high-end culinary school set in Jerusalem, and this branding project focused on creating a full visual identity that felt grounded in the culture of the region while still appealing to a global audience of students. The work included a new mascot logo based on the markhor, a 12 page merchandise catalog, and a set of collectible stickers inspired by passport and postage stamps. The goal was to build a brand that felt modern, confident, and meaningful, using elements of local culture, symbolism, and design history to create something students would connect with and feel proud to represent. Every part of the system, from the geometric shapes of the mascot to the use of two Pantone spot colors, needed to reinforce a unified visual language that could live across physical merchandise, print layouts, and promotional materials.

The goal was to build a brand that felt modern, confident, and meaningful, using elements of local culture, symbolism, and design history to create something students would connect with and feel proud to represent. Every part of the system, from the geometric shapes of the mascot to the use of two Pantone spot colors, needed to reinforce a unified visual language that could live across physical merchandise, print layouts, and promotional materials.

children.name: The biggest challenge of this project was figuring out how to blend the cultural richness of Jerusalem with a design style that felt contemporary enough for an international student audience. The brand needed to respect the history and traditions of the region without looking overly literal or dated, which meant finding a balance between authenticity and visual simplicity. Another difficulty was shaping the markhor mascot into something that could resonate with students from a variety of backgrounds, since it needed to feel iconic and strong but also approachable enough to work on apparel and merchandise. On a broader level, the new identity had to set Spierer University apart from well established culinary institutions around the world by highlighting the school’s unique cultural setting and its emphasis on global learning, community, and hands on expertise.

children.name: Research included a deep look into Jerusalem’s architecture, wildlife, food culture, and visual history to help ground the brand in a specific sense of place. The markhor, which appears in regions connected to the Middle East, became an anchor for the brand because it represents resilience, adaptability, and tradition, all qualities tied closely to culinary education. I also studied global culinary schools to understand how they present prestige and identity, noting that many focus heavily on technical mastery but often lack cultural depth, which gave Spierer University an opportunity to stand out through stronger storytelling. Audience research showed that students value community, innovation, and a sense of belonging, which pushed the design direction toward something that feels rooted yet modern. This mix of cultural references, geometric simplification, and bold visual clarity shaped the foundation for the final brand.

children.name: The final identity uses a stylized geometric markhor as the centerpiece, colored with two Pantone spot colors for clarity, versatility, and strong brand recognition. The mascot was designed to feel simple and iconic so it could work on everything from shirts and chef jackets to catalogs and stickers. The 12 page catalog presents merchandise in a clear, organized way that shows off the school’s personality through layout, product photography, and small visual details tied to the brand values of creativity and professionalism. The sticker set takes inspiration from travel ephemera like passport stamps and postage marks, each design celebrating local culture through shapes, motifs, and references to Jerusalem and the surrounding region. One sticker integrates the golden ratio as a subtle nod to craft and precision. Altogether, the visual system feels bold, contemporary, and grounded in place, giving Spierer University a distinctive identity that students and alumni would want to engage with and represent.

Another difficulty was shaping the markhor mascot into something that could resonate with students from a variety of backgrounds, since it needed to feel iconic and strong but also approachable enough to work on apparel and merchandise. On a broader level, the new identity had to set Spierer University apart from well established culinary institutions around the world by highlighting the school’s unique cultural setting and its emphasis on global learning, community, and hands on expertise.

This mix of cultural references, geometric simplification, and bold visual clarity shaped the foundation for the final brand.

The 12 page catalog presents merchandise in a clear, organized way that shows off the school’s personality through layout, product photography, and small visual details tied to the brand values of creativity and professionalism. The sticker set takes inspiration from travel ephemera like passport stamps and postage marks, each design celebrating local culture through shapes, motifs, and references to Jerusalem and the surrounding region. Altogether, the visual system feels bold, contemporary, and grounded in place, giving Spierer University a distinctive identity that students and alumni would want to engage with and represent.
